naming_rules.backend_order_name: The source label (folder name and file-name prefix, e.g. 'LightPink 41/100'). This is how Robert finds the supplier listing when a customer orders. Never rename it; keep the N/100 suffix verbatim.
naming_rules.color_folder: One subfolder per color, named by the color label (e.g. 'Green 12/100').
naming_rules.photo_files: Named <label>-front.jpg, <label>-back.jpg (plus -detail, -model-front, etc. when more views exist), where <label> is the source label lowercased with spaces as hyphens.

photo_rules.hoodies: First 2 carousel photos (front + back) unless told otherwise for that item.
photo_rules.sneakers: Up to 3 pics per color from reverse image search; first online source's other views first; 2 if 3 cannot be found, 1 if 2 cannot be found; cropped DHGate photo only as a last resort.

naming_rules.public_facing_name: The real product name (the 'public_name' field here, and the tracker sheet's 'Real product name' column). This is the name the website shows customers. It must match the photo.
naming_rules.store_folder: The folder directly under each brand folder IS the store name — the supplier (usually DHGate) store the item is ordered from (e.g. damai2023, casualyn, museround27). The 'store' field on every item repeats it. When an order comes in, use store + source_label + source_link together to find the exact listing to order from. If store is TBD, the store is not known yet and the order cannot be placed until it is found.
naming_rules.source_color_name: The color name the supplier store uses for the item (e.g. 'Green 12/100'). This is the name to use when ordering — it often does NOT describe the garment's real color (the 'Green 12/100' garment is black). Record it exactly as the store shows it, next to the real color, so the two are never confused.
naming_rules.ordering: An order needs three things together: store name + source label + source link, where source link is the DHGate listing (recorded in the tracker sheet, never in this repo). The public-facing name is for customers only, never for ordering. The photo reference link is never part of an order.
naming_rules.color_identifier: The color word from the source label, on its own (e.g. 'LightPink', 'Green', 'Black'). This is the color name the supplier store uses for the item — it often does NOT describe the garment's real color. Use it with the numbering to identify the exact store variant.
naming_rules.numbering: The item's number within the store's listing, written as N/100 (e.g. '41/100' means item 41 out of 100). It is the second half of the source label: 'LightPink 41/100' splits into color identifier 'LightPink' + numbering '41/100'. Record it exactly as shown; if a listing has no numbering, leave it blank.
naming_rules.per_item_record: Every product carries: store name, source link (DHGate ordering link, when available), color identifier, and numbering (when available). The photo reference link is a separate fifth field and is never an ordering source. The two links live in the tracker sheet only — this repo carries the store, color identifier, and numbering. Together with the source label they identify the exact store variant to order.
naming_rules.source_link: The ordering link ONLY: the DHGate listing (or YUPOO category for the Purple Brand drop) where the item is bought. It lives ONLY in the tracker sheet (Source link column) — never in this repo. Never a Grailed, Vestiaire, Editorialist, Saks, StockX, or Reversible link — those are photo references, not sources. Empty in the tracker means the DHGate ordering link has not been provided yet.
naming_rules.photo_reference_link: Where the real, unedited photo was found (Grailed, Vestiaire Collective, Editorialist, Saks, StockX, Reversible, Kering DAM, etc.). It lives ONLY in the tracker sheet (Photo reference link column) — never in this repo. This link exists ONLY to show where the public-facing photo came from — it is NOT a source and must NEVER be used to order. The photo itself is the product image customers see; the link is provenance only.
naming_rules.retail_price: Leave retail_price_usd EMPTY unless the user provides the price himself. NEVER take the price from a photo-reference link (Grailed, Vestiaire, Editorialist, Reversible, Saks, StockX, MR PORTER, etc.) — the price on those pages is irrelevant. The user will give prices later.
